This run followed ~20+ minutes of cold nix devShell provisioning immediately beforehand, and pass 2's 1666s for only 19 selected items (~88s/test) is anomalous against its own 1800s budget for what should be a light serial pass -- circumstantially consistent with residual I/O/CPU contention bleeding into the test run rather than a real regression, but this is NOT proven and must not be assumed. A second, clean data point (idle machine, warm devShell) is needed to distinguish the two before concluding either way.

Phase 5 landed no net source change and Phase 6's only change is the marker itself -- there is no code change in this task's own diff that could mechanically explain these 19 failures, which further supports (but does not prove) the contention-artifact reading over a task-176-caused regression.

If the failures reproduce on a clean re-run, they are out of this task's stated scope (task 176 is scoped specifically to test_shift_closure_on_extracted_worlds_m3) and the correct move is very likely a new spawned follow-up task, not fixing them inside task 176 -- but do not take that action without the clean re-run confirming reproduction first.
